[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] The New York Stock Exchanges primary data center sits in Mahwah, New Jersey, now owned and operated by Intercontinental Exchange, Inc., listed on the NYSE itself under ticker ICE, which acquired NYSE Euronext for approximately 8.2 billion dollars in a deal announced December 19, 2012. The facility was designed around five 20,000 square foot modules totaling 100,000 square feet of modular data hall space within an approximately 400,000 square foot building footprint, with 28 megawatts of total power capacity, brought online in stages over roughly two years before the ICE acquisition closed. The Mahwah facility was part of a broader NYSE infrastructure consolidation that reduced the exchanges footprint from eight data centers, six in the US and two in Europe, down to two primary sites, Mahwah and Basildon in the United Kingdom. The facility houses NYSEs electronic trading matching engines and offers colocation services to high-frequency trading firms seeking the lowest possible latency to the exchanges order matching systems, a specialized niche distinct from general enterprise or cloud colocation. Today the site operates under ICEs broader colocation and connectivity business, marketed as ICE Global Network and Colocation, which publishes detailed technical specifications for prospective colocation tenants. This facility is recorded under the operator name nyse in this registry, treated as the same entity as NYSE (Intercontinental Exchange, ICE) researched at the operator level. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.
